answer:
## FINAL ANSWER (hypothesis, ready to submit)

**Interval label: 1985–1990.** Among black females (pooled, **n = 1,548**, all 1,548 observed in each of the three waves), median composite wealth was **$175 in 1985 → $2,600 in 1990 → $4,000 in 1996**. Both intervals are increases, but the larger absolute increase is **1985→1990: +$2,425**, versus **1990→1996: +$1,400** — a point difference of **$1,025**. Support % column: +1,385.7% (1985–1990) and +53.8% (1990–1996); the first percentage is *not meaningful* because the base median of $175 is effectively zero. **The conclusion is not robust to how exact-zero wealth values are handled**: treating zeros as technical missing (medians $3,832 → $8,100 → $19,800; +$4,268 vs +$11,700) or keeping only positive wealth ($4,800 → $11,057 → $25,050; +$6,257 vs +$13,993) both reverse the ranking and give **1990–1996** as the largest increase — and there it wins on both the absolute and the relative criterion. Honest formulation: under a literal reading of the composite wealth variables the biggest median gain is **1985–1990**, but that ordering is produced by the zero-coding rule; under either alternative reading the answer is **1990–1996**.

## Evidence (from analysis/results_report.txt, analysis/results_table.csv)

| branch | interval | median A | median B | Δ $ | Δ % | direction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRIMARY (zeros kept, no dedup) | 1985–1990 | 175 | 2,600 | **+2,425** | +1,385.7% (not meaningful) | increase |
| PRIMARY | 1990–1996 | 2,600 | 4,000 | +1,400 | +53.8% | increase |
| SENS-1 (zeros→NaN) | 1985–1990 | 3,832 (n=930) | 8,100 (n=1,093) | +4,268 | +111.4% | increase |
| SENS-1 | 1990–1996 | 8,100 | 19,800 (n=1,057) | **+11,700** | +144.4% | increase |
| SENS-2 (positive only) | 1985–1990 | 4,800 (n=813) | 11,057 (n=978) | +6,257 | +130.4% | increase |
| SENS-2 | 1990–1996 | 11,057 | 25,050 (n=956) | **+13,993** | +126.6% | increase |

Margin between the two deltas: $1,025 (primary), $7,432 (SENS-1), $7,736 (SENS-2) — the sensitivity branches are far more decisive than the primary branch, which is itself a reason not to over-read the primary winner.

Why it's fragile: black-female zero share is 39.9% (1985), 29.4% (1990), 31.7% (1996); the share at or below $0 is 47.5%/36.8%/38.2%, so the 1985 median sits *at the edge of the zero block* — exactly the configuration that inflates the apparent 1985→1990 jump. 231 black females report 0 in all three waves. Cross-group evidence that zeros are partly technical: white respondents go 20.7%/20.3% → **42.6%** and 24.6%/25.7% → **43.3%** zeros in 1996, a within-group doubling that is implausible as real asset loss.

Other required checks: n per year is 1,548/1,548/1,548 (complete-case ≡ all-available, so that choice is moot). ever_jailed==1 has n=16 with medians $0/$0/$0 — picture is uninterpretable at n=16 and was not used. One bootstrap (B=2,000, seed 20261023, primary branch, resampling respondents): P(1985–1990 wins)=96.6%, P(1990–1996)=3.1%, ties 0.2% — sampling noise is *not* the source of disagreement; the zero-handling rule is.

## Limitations
Nominal dollars, no inflation adjustment (a 1985→1996 level comparison embeds ~40–50% price growth); no weights/strata/PSU in the file, so every figure is a point estimate with no confidence interval; no respondent ID, so "one row = one respondent" and the decision to keep the 1,899 exact-duplicate rows stay unverifiable assumptions; the file contains only 1985/1990/1996 wealth, so only these two intervals were ever candidates.

payload.hypothesis: Interval label: 1985-1990. Among pooled black females (n=1,548; 1,548 respondents observed in each of 1985, 1990 and 1996) median composite wealth rose from $175 in 1985 to $2,600 in 1990 and to $4,000 in 1996, so both candidate intervals are increases and the larger absolute increase occurred between 1985 and 1990 (+$2,425) rather than between 1990 and 1996 (+$1,400), a point difference of $1,025. The supporting percentage changes are +1,385.7% for 1985-1990 and +53.8% for 1990-1996, but the 1985-1990 percentage is not meaningful because the 1985 median of $175 is effectively zero. This conclusion is not robust to how exact-zero wealth values are handled: treating zeros as technical missing (medians $3,832 -> $8,100 -> $19,800; +$4,268 vs +$11,700) or restricting to positive wealth ($4,800 -> $11,057 -> $25,050; +$6,257 vs +$13,993) both reverse the ranking and give 1990-1996 as the interval with the largest increase, on both the absolute and the relative criterion. The 1985-1990 result therefore rests on 39.9% zero-coded 1985 wealth values and on the 1985 median sitting at the edge of a block in which 47.5% of black females are at or below $0; 231 black females report 0 wealth in all three waves, and zero shares roughly double in 1996 for white respondents (20.7/20.3 -> 42.6% and 24.6/25.7 -> 43.3%), which suggests part of the zeros are technical rather than real. A single bootstrap (B=2,000, primary branch) leaves 1985-1990 winning with probability 96.6%, so sampling noise is not what drives the disagreement - the zero-handling rule is. All estimates are unweighted, nominal-dollar point estimates (no weights or variance information exist in the file), no inflation adjustment is applied, rows are assumed to be distinct respondents without deduplication, and the stratification by ever_jailed is not interpretable (n=16).
payload.workflow: 1) Inspection pass (analysis/inspect_data.py -> analysis/inspection_report.txt): schema, exact label spellings, race x sex counts, missingness, zero/negative mass, confirmation that only composite_wealth_1985/1990/1996 exist (hence exactly two candidate intervals). 2) Filter race=='black' & sex=='female' (lowercase exact match), n=1,548; n identical in all three years, so complete-case vs all-available is moot. 3) PRIMARY branch per ruling (b): zeros kept as real zero wealth, no deduplication; median per year; absolute $ delta per interval as the ranking criterion per ruling (a); % delta as a support column with an explicit flag when the base median is ~0. 4) Two equal-weight sensitivity branches: zeros->NaN and positive-wealth-only, same interval logic. 5) Report BOTH intervals in every branch with medians, $ delta, % delta and sign; explicitly flag that the winning interval changes between branches. 6) Exactly one bootstrap run (B=2,000, seed 20261023, primary branch, resampling the 1,548 respondents) for rank stability, one conclusion. 7) ever_jailed==1 reported as a one-liner (n=16, medians $0/$0/$0, not interpretable). Outputs: analysis/results_report.txt, analysis/results_table.csv, analysis/black_female_distribution_by_year.csv, analysis/hypothesis.md.
